root_cause: The initial ProRes RAW decoder implementation (decode_comp) assumed that every tile, including the rightmost/edge tiles, has a visible width of at least 16 pixels (enough to produce at least one 8x-wide block for the clz-based log2 computation), but no validation enforces this assumption on attacker-controlled width/tile values, allowing nb_blocks to become 0 and reach an invalid __builtin_clz(0) call.
findings: In decode_comp(), the local visible tile width is computed as `w = FFMIN(s->tw, avctx->width - tile->x) / 2`, and then `nb_blocks = w / 8` is derived from it. `nb_blocks` is subsequently passed to `ff_clz()` (which wraps `__builtin_clz`) via `log2_nb_blocks = 31 - ff_clz(nb_blocks)`. `__builtin_clz(0)` is undefined behavior per the GCC/Clang documentation because it does not have a well-defined re
